_comment: The eight priority subjects, seeded as DRAFTS. Every record deliberately omits baseline, target, target date, actions and evidence: none of those exist from a verified public source yet, and a tracker that opens with invented numbers is worse than one that opens empty. The detail template renders 'Baseline not yet established from a verified public source.' wherever a field is absent. The office fills these in as real figures and real actions become available, each with its own source URL and verification date.
_historical_targets: Every record is flagged campaign_origin: true, but historical_target is EMPTY on all eight. The original 2026 campaign wording is not in this repository and was not available to transcribe. Do not write it from memory. Retrieve it from the archived campaign site or the campaign's own records, paste it verbatim into historical_target, and it will render under a label marking it as historical context rather than a current commitment.
_governance_note: The role, direct_control, influence and district_context fields describe what any individual Board member can and cannot do. They contain no claim about anything T. L. Harris has personally done. The nine-member composition of the Board is from https://www.scsk12.org/board/ (accessed 2026-09-20). The rest is governance framing and needs office review before publication.
_status_note: All eight open as 'Not Started', which is the accurate description of a tracker with no recorded baseline and no recorded action. The office sets real statuses as work begins.

priorities.title: Early Literacy and Third-Grade Reading
priorities.description: Third-grade reading proficiency across Memphis-Shelby County Schools, and what the Board asks about it.
priorities.why_it_matters: Reading by the end of third grade shapes how a student experiences every subject that comes after it.
priorities.role: One of nine elected members of the Memphis-Shelby County Schools Board of Education.
priorities.direct_control: How he votes on items that come before the Board. What he asks for in Board meetings and puts on the public record. What he reports back to District 6.
priorities.influence: Which issues get Board discussion and how often. Requests for data and public reporting. Advocacy with colleagues and the administration.
priorities.district_context: Reading outcomes depend on classroom instruction, school leadership and district-wide programmes. The Board acts as a body, and any single member's vote is one of nine.

priorities.title: Early Literacy Instruction and Structured Literacy
priorities.description: How reading is taught in the early grades, and which instructional approach the district uses.
priorities.why_it_matters: The method used to teach reading is what decides whether early gaps close or widen.
priorities.role: One of nine elected members of the Memphis-Shelby County Schools Board of Education.
priorities.direct_control: How he votes on curriculum and budget items that reach the Board. What he asks about instructional practice in public session.
priorities.influence: Whether instructional approach is discussed at Board level, and what reporting the Board requests on it.
priorities.district_context: Curriculum selection and teacher training are run by district administration. A Board member does not set classroom practice.

priorities.title: Early Intervention
priorities.description: How quickly students who fall behind are identified, and what support follows.
priorities.why_it_matters: Support given early costs less and works better than support given late.
priorities.role: One of nine elected members of the Memphis-Shelby County Schools Board of Education.
priorities.direct_control: How he votes on programmes and funding that come before the Board. What he asks about identification and support in public session.
priorities.influence: Whether intervention data is reported to the Board and made public.
priorities.district_context: Identification and support happen at school level, under district programmes. Some requirements come from outside the district.

priorities.title: School Improvement Goals
priorities.description: Improvement targets set for schools in the district, and the Board's oversight of progress against them.
priorities.why_it_matters: Improvement goals are how a district states publicly what it is trying to change.
priorities.role: One of nine elected members of the Memphis-Shelby County Schools Board of Education.
priorities.direct_control: How he votes on goals and plans presented to the Board. What he asks for in the way of progress reporting.
priorities.influence: How regularly progress is reviewed in public session.
priorities.district_context: Goals are set and carried out by district and school leadership. The Board's role is oversight, exercised as a body.

priorities.title: Safe and Supportive Learning Environments
priorities.description: School climate, behavioural standards, and the support available to students and staff.
priorities.why_it_matters: Students learn where they feel safe, and staff stay where schools are well run.
priorities.role: One of nine elected members of the Memphis-Shelby County Schools Board of Education.
priorities.direct_control: How he votes on policy that comes before the Board. What he raises publicly about school conditions in District 6.
priorities.influence: Whether climate and discipline data is reported to the Board and published.
priorities.district_context: Day-to-day discipline and safety are handled by school leadership under district policy. A Board member does not manage staff or individual student matters.

priorities.title: Annual Literacy Growth Reports
priorities.description: Whether literacy progress is reported publicly each year, in a form residents can actually read.
priorities.why_it_matters: A commitment nobody reports on cannot be checked by anyone.
priorities.role: One of nine elected members of the Memphis-Shelby County Schools Board of Education.
priorities.direct_control: What he asks the district to report. What he publishes to District 6 through this site, whether or not the district publishes its own.
priorities.influence: Whether the Board requests annual public reporting on literacy.
priorities.district_context: District-wide reporting is produced by the administration. What this office can do on its own is publish what it has, and say plainly what it does not have.

priorities.title: Quarterly Town Halls
priorities.description: Regular public meetings in District 6 where residents can raise concerns directly.
priorities.why_it_matters: Residents need a predictable place to raise something and be answered in public.
priorities.role: One of nine elected members of the Memphis-Shelby County Schools Board of Education.
priorities.direct_control: Whether the meetings are scheduled and held. Whether a summary is published afterwards. What follow-up is recorded.
priorities.influence: Whether concerns raised at a town hall reach the district and get a response.
priorities.district_context: Holding the meetings is within this office's own control. Attendance, and what the district does in response to what is raised, are not.

priorities.title: Public Performance Dashboard
priorities.description: Whether district performance information is published in one place the public can find and use.
priorities.why_it_matters: Information the public cannot find cannot hold anyone to account.
priorities.role: One of nine elected members of the Memphis-Shelby County Schools Board of Education.
priorities.direct_control: What this office publishes and keeps current on this site.
priorities.influence: Whether the district builds or improves its own public reporting.
priorities.district_context: A district-wide dashboard would be built and maintained by the district. Any figure shown here must come from a published district or state source, with that source named.
